items.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
items.summary: Neocloud Lambda has raised $1B in private debt to buy Nvidia AI chips and lease them to Microsoft. It's the latest in a string of loans, underscoring the high cost of the AI boom.

items.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
items.summary: Given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviors, the automated systems were able to improve performance on every single one without degrading overall performance.

items.title: Brave’s browser one-ups Chrome with its new support for email aliases
items.summary: The feature, announced this week, allows Brave's users to sign up for websites and other online services without having to share their personal email addresses.

items.title: Open-weight AI companies are the Valley’s hottest acquisition targets
items.summary: There's a lot of capital pouring into the business of giving models away.

items.title: How Sweden built one of Europe’s hottest startup ecosystems
items.summary: Sophia Bendz, general partner at Cherry Ventures, stopped by Equity to break down the latest in the Swedish tech ecosystem.

items.title: More Americans oppose police license plate cameras than support them: survey
items.summary: The backlash against license plate readers comes amid a wave of police abuses of surveillance cameras.

items.title: Friend-focused photo-sharing app Retro snags $21M
items.summary: Retro, a friend-focused photo-sharing app built by former Instagram employees, has raised more than $21 million in Series A funding.

items.title: Apple TV is raising its subscription prices again
items.summary: Now, Apple TV subscriptions will cost $14.99 per month, up from its previous price of $12.99 per month.

items.title: a16z creates a $1.1B ‘Machine Age’ fund to ‘accelerate the physical buildout of AI’
items.summary: The firm, known for its focus on software, is going to start throwing more money at the hardware behind AI.

items.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply-chain risk label
items.summary: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk, handing the AI company a victory as its second Pentagon lawsuit continues in Washington.

items.title: Meta executive leaves for OpenAI as the social media giant faces growing scrutiny in India
items.summary: Sandhya Devanathan will oversee some OpenAI operations across Southeast Asia and Australia in her new role.

items.title: As electric two-wheelers gain a foothold, Belgian startup Any bets on cargo space
items.summary: Launched by Belgian startup Any, LUV1 is a modular electric motorcycle with 120 liters of cargo space that can be used to carry bags, work equipment, or even pets.

items.title: AI, athletes, and Keith Rabois: StrictlyVC is back in New York on September 10
items.summary: A boutique StrictlyVC evening returns to New York's West Village on September 10 with Keith Rabois, Craig Shapiro, Jason Levien, Tristan Walker, Brynn Putnam, and Deven Parekh — covering AI, sports investing, community-building, venture economics, and politics, with cocktails, food, and networking throughout the night.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are joining the AI stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
items.summary: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, the AI Stage is back to dig into the single hottest topic in the community for the past few years, presented by Google for Startups.

items.title: Rivian’s CFO is leaving the company
items.summary: Claire McDonough is stepping down on October 30 to pursue a new opportunity, the company said in a filing on Thursday.

items.title: Bluesky adds an ‘algorithmic opt-out’ feature for those who don’t want to go viral
items.summary: Sometimes people just want to post to their followers, Bluesky says.

items.title: Buried in Meta’s $18B settlement is a legal pass on kids’ data
items.summary: Meta’s settlement with 29 states allows it to retain certain data from children under 13 to train and test age-detection models, highlighting a privacy trade-off built into the deal.

items.title: YouTube now lets creators tag Amazon products and earn commissions from purchases
items.summary: The update turns product recommendations into a more direct revenue stream for creators, and for Amazon, the move puts its massive online marketplace inside one of the most popular video platforms.

items.title: Barret Zoph, the Thinking Machines co-founder ousted before joining OpenAI, is now at Google
items.summary: Zoph, who co-founded Thinking Machines Lab alongside Mira Murati and also served as the startup's CTO, led a brief stint at OpenAI and is now at Google.

items.title: ATF declares ‘major incident’ as ransomware gang claims hack
items.summary: The ATF is the latest federal government agency in recent years to notify Congress of a "major incident" involving its cybersecurity.
